summary: Perceived inference slowdowns and intermittent request timeouts — client SDK retries + connection pool misconfiguration
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightCompose reported sudden increase in end-to-end response times and occasional 504/timeout errors when calling the Redwood API from their backend. Impact started 2026-03-10 ~11:20 UTC and affected multiple production services that rely on synchronous generation calls.

Impact:
- User-facing feature latency increased from ~120ms median token latency to >800ms for some requests.
- Intermittent request timeouts (504) observed, customer reported retries compounding the load.
- Bulk of traffic routed to dedicated capacity pool in us-east.

Environment:
- Customer: BrightCompose (dedicated plan)
- Region: prod-us-east
- SDK: redwood-sdk v2.0.1 (node)
- Network: Kubernetes cluster behind gateway, Node.js backend using axios + keep-alive agent

Steps to reproduce:
1) Send batch of 100 concurrent generate requests from customer backend to Redwood hosted API in us-east with model gpt-redwood-13b.
2) Observe increased tail latency and occasional timeouts when concurrency rises above ~40.

Observed behavior:
- Requests pile up on the customer side and show long connect/idle times in traces.
- Server-side metrics for serving-runtime show normal CPU/GPU utilisation but short bursts of elevated connection churn.
- Customer logs show aggressive retry attempts with minimal backoff configured in their SDK wrapper, leading to request storms.

Expected behavior:
- Stable latency under the committed capacity and graceful retries that do not amplify load.

Key logs / snippets (customer-provided):
- Client side timing breakdowns show high TCP connection setup times and many sockets in TIME_WAIT.
- Customer tracer: connect_time dominated tail latency (connect: 400ms+), request_time lower once connected.
- SDK config excerpt: retries=5, backoff_ms=100, max_sockets=4 (per-host), keepAlive=false
comments: 2026-03-10 12:05 UTC — Aisha Patel (Support): Acknowledged and triaged. Escalated to infra/SRE for investigation. Created linked INT ticket for internal investigation (INT-423).

2026-03-10 12:28 UTC — Miguel Santos (SRE): Initial findings — serving-runtime healthy, error % not elevated on our side. Seeing increased short-lived connections from BrightCompose host IPs. Asking customer for SDK config and netstat output.

2026-03-10 12:46 UTC — BrightCompose (customer): Provided node app info and netstat. Confirmed they upgraded to redwood-sdk v2.0.1 last week and recently rolled a change that sets keepAlive=false to 'avoid socket reuse issues'.

2026-03-10 13:10 UTC — Miguel Santos (SRE): Hypothesis posted — client-side connection churn + aggressive retry/backoff causing perceived latency. Recommended temporary configs to customer (enable keep-alive, increase max sockets, add jitter to backoff, lower retry attempts).

2026-03-10 14:50 UTC — BrightCompose: Applied suggested config (keepAlive=true, max_sockets=50, retries=2, backoff_ms=300-1200 jitter). Observed immediate reduction in connect times and tail latency. Confirmed no 504s in the following hour.
2026-03-11 09:00 UTC — Engineering (SDK): Opened PR to change default v2.x SDK behavior to enable HTTP keep-alive and sensible default connection pool sizing. PR linked in ticket.
2026-03-12 11:45 UTC — BrightCompose: Verified stable performance for 24+ hours. Marked incident as resolved from their side.
investigation_notes: Checked serving-runtime metrics: GPU/CPU utilization within normal bounds for dedicated pool, no backend queueing on model workers.
Correlated remote IPs: same customer IP range showed high rate of short-lived TCP connections and a spike in TIME_WAIT states on our edge proxies.
Traces show connect latency dominating tail; once connection established token generation latency was normal — points to client-side connection churn rather than model slowness.
Customer SDK snapshot revealed keepAlive=false and very low max_sockets (4) which caused serializing connection attempts under moderate concurrency while retries multiplied outstanding requests.
Reproduced locally using customer's config: synthetic load replicated high tail latency when client keep-alive disabled and retries aggressive (5x, 100ms backoff).
Runbook cross-check: behavior matches known anti-pattern documented in SDK Connection Pool Best Practices.
resolution_notes: Root cause: Customer SDK configuration (keepAlive disabled + very small connection pool) combined with aggressive retry/backoff (short fixed backoff and high retry count) created connection storms and queueing at the gateway, causing perceived inference latency and intermittent timeouts.

Immediate mitigation provided to customer: re-enable HTTP keep-alive, increase per-host max sockets, reduce retry attempts, and add exponential backoff with jitter. Customer applied changes and confirmed improvement.

Medium-term fix: SDK team merged PR to change defaults in redwood-sdk v2.1.3 — enable keep-alive by default, increase recommended maxSockets, add exponential backoff with full jitter and sensible default retry count.

Follow-ups: create a short KB article for customers on SDK connection tuning (confluence page linked), add a warning to Console’s Dedicated capacity dashboard when we observe high connection churn from a single customer, and add an automated detection rule to SRE alerts to flag high TIME_WAIT/connection churn from dedicated pools.
Customer verified recovery and requested closure. Ticket resolved 2026-03-12.
